data.name: Silian
data.gender_notes: Silian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Silian is derived from the Latin name Silas, which was derived from the Greek name Silas. Silas was a prominent disciple of Saint Paul in the New Testament, and is considered to be one of the seventy-two disciples. Silas is also believed to have carried Paul and Barnabas' letters to various Christian communities in Greece and Asia Minor. The name Silas is derived from the Greek word silas, which means 'foreman' or 'ruler'. In the religious context, Silas represents leadership and authority in the service of the Lord.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes leadership and authority in the service of the Lord.
data.etymology: Silian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “From Silas.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Silian total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_greek.name: Σιλιαν
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Σιλιαν προέρχεται από το λατινικό και σημαίνει δάσος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σιλιαν έχει τις ρίζες του στη λατινική γλώσσα και σχετίζεται με το δάσος. Στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία, τα ονόματα που σχετίζονταν με τη φύση είχαν συχνά πνευματική σημασία. in_english.long_meaning: The Christian name Silian, derived from Latin roots, signifies 'forest' or 'woods,' symbolizing a connection to nature and, by extension, to spiritual growth and divine creation. The name Silian, with its connotations of serenity and abundance found in forests, may inspire qualities of peace, growth, and harmony in those who bear it.

data.cultural_impact: Silian as a Christian name carries with it a rich cultural heritage, not only from the Latin and Greek origins, but also from the significant role of Saint Silas in early Christianity. As a name, Silian invokes images of strong leadership and authority, a reminder of Silas' prominence as one of the seventy-two disciples and his essential role in spreading the Gospel.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Silian holds deep spiritual significance for Christians, representing the call to be a leader and servant of the Lord. Silas, being an influential figure in early Christianity, reminds us of the importance of spreading the teachings of the faith and living a life of service to those around us. The name Silian is a reminder to be a foreman in our own lives, overseeing our thoughts, words, and actions in accordance with God's will, and leading others by example towards a closer relationship with Him.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Silian is a name derived from the Celtic word "sil," meaning sun. In Christian symbolism, Silian represents the light of God shining upon an individual, illuminating their path and guiding them through life's challenges. The name also embodies the idea of God's infinite and eternal power, as the sun is a symbol of God's divine presence and constancy.

biblical_reference.note: The name Silian does not have a direct biblical reference but is influenced by Latin and used in Christian tradition.

historical_references.reference: Saint Silian of Perugia, also known as Silian of Assisi, was a Christian martyr who lived during the late Roman period. He was a deacon in the city of Perugia and was executed by the Romans around the year 304 due to his refusal to renounce his faith. Silian is considered a local patron saint of Perugia and his feast day is celebrated on December 8.

Saint Silian of Scythia was a Christian martyr who lived during the 3rd century. He is said to have been a bishop in Scythia, present-day Romania, and was martyred during the reign of Emperor Decius (249-251 AD). According to legend, Silian was tortured and beheaded, along with several other Christian bishops and deacons, for refusing to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods.
